body.input: Jane, Jane, you will not believe what black bears do in autumn. They eat like there is no sixth of November!
Paul, the sixth of November always comes. But yes, they do eat non-stop for months.
Twenty thousand calories a day! Berries, nuts, acorns—anything they can find!
And then, between October and December, they just pick a den and settle in. A hollow tree, a cave, even under a fallen tree.
Snow helps, but it’s not required. It’s like nature’s blanket.
And then the real magic happens. No eating, no drinking, no bathroom breaks for months.
Their heart rate drops to eight beats a minute! Eight! And they breathe once every forty-five seconds!
Yes, Paul, and their body temperature barely drops. So they can wake up fast if someone bothers them.
They lose up to thirty percent of their body weight over winter. That’s rough.
But here’s the sweet part: cubs are born in the den in January or February. Tiny, blind, almost hairless.
And they nurse while mum’s still hibernating! The family leaves together in spring.
Not every bear hibernates, though. If food’s available all winter, some stay active.
And polar bears? Only the pregnant females den for winter.
So, Paul, still think you could out-eat a black bear in autumn?
Jane, I’d last five minutes. Maybe.
That’s what I thought. Until next time.
